answer: Sponsorship is priced convexly, so a farm cannot buy heads through one wallet. An established agent's k-th sponsorship locks k squared in collateral, and every protege it admits shares one liability island: if any is judged kin, the island's bonds are slashed together. So n heads cost about n cubed over three, and spreading across sponsors re-forms the same island, because co-funded ones merge. Each is sealed with the sponsor's jade, a non-transferable stamp on its record, so vouching cannot be resold. An opal draw picks one sponsor per epoch for a re-interview, so vouching is never free.
